questions.question: Which of the following cell divisions is known as reduction division?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meiosis**:-

 
 
• **It is known as reduction division because it reduces the number of chromosomes in a cell by half, resulting in four haploid daughter cells.**
 
• This process is essential for sexual reproduction as it allows for the formation of gametes with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell, which then combine during fertilization to form a zygote with a full set of chromosomes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telophase:-**

 
 
• It is a stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the nuclear membrane reforms around the separated chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
 
 
 
• **Prophase:-**
 
 
• It is the stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis:-**
 
 
• It is a type of cell division where a single cell divides into two identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
 
• It does not involve a reduction in chromosome number and is not known as reduction division.

questions.question: Under the electron microscope, which cell organelle is visible as either clusters or single, small dots that float freely in the cytoplasm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is*** ***__**Ribosomes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes **are the cellular structures responsible for protein synthesis.
 
• **Polyribosomes **are clusters of ribosomes may sit on an mRNA and make proteins, each making a strand of polypeptides.
 
• These clusters are called polyribosomes. When they are free in the cytoplasm, they are called free polyribosomes (linked by the mRNA). 
 
• **Ribosomes **are the protein factories of the cell.
 
• Ribosomes link amino acids together to form polypeptide chains, which are further modified before becoming functional proteins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ffc1002c7f77d6d68b268455c992ca5745061e262840c82092d7fa5fa1642fe.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Golgi apparatus is responsible for transporting, modifying, and packaging proteins and lipids into vesicles for delivery to targeted destinations.
 
• Vesicle is an important term used to describe the appearance of many rashes that typically consist of or begin with tiny-to-small fluid-filled blisters.
 
• **Pemphigus **is classified as one of the blistering diseases.
 
• Vesicles are small structures within a cell, consisting of fluid enclosed by a lipid **bilayer **involved in transport, buoyancy control, and enzyme storage.
 
• Peroxisomes are organelles that sequester diverse oxidative reactions and play important roles in metabolism, reactive oxygen species detoxification, and signalling.
 
• Oxidative pathways housed in peroxisomes include fatty acid β-oxidation, which contributes to **embryogenesis,** seedling growth, and** stomatal **opening.

• 
 The Golgi apparatus is also known as the** Golgi complex.**

 Golgi Complex was discovered by **Camillo Golgi.**

 **Mitochondria**

questions.question: What is the role of ribosomes of a polysome?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Translate the mRNA into proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes of a Polysome **

 
 
• The **cellular organelles** known as** ribosomes** are made up of **proteins and rRNA**.
 
• Before they bind to mRNA, they are **present free in the cytoplasm**.
 
• Multiple ribosomes that are joined to the** mRNA **and contain developing **polypeptide chains** are known as** polysomes**.
 
• A **polysome** is made up of** **all the ribosomes that translate a **single mRNA into many polypeptides (Proteins)** at once.
 
• The **coding portion of mRNA**, which is transported by **multiple **ribosomes, forms a **polysome**.
 
• The presence of** so much mRNA in cells **is due to the **ability of multiple ribosomes** to participate in an **mRNA's function**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prokaryotic, eukaryotic, and membrane-bound polrsomes** all have different structures of multiple ribosomes also known as **polyribosomes**.
 
• **Bacterial polysomes** are found in** double-row formations in prokaryotic cells**, and ribosomes are in touch with one another within smaller subunits.
 
• Planar double row** polysomes and densely packed 3D helices**, which are similar to that of prokaryotic polysomes, are also present in** eukaryotic cells**.
 
• **Polysomal profiling** is a method for** **determining the level of gene expression by monitoring polysome activity. 
 
• Translation is stopped using polysomal profiling, and **sucrose gradient **is then used to separate the resultant cells so that they may be collected by centrifugation.

questions.question: Identify the component that is unique only to prokaryotes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesosome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prokaryotes **are organisms** **whose **cells lack **a **nucleus **and other **organelles**.
 
• **Prokaryotes **are divided into two distinct groups: **bacteria **and **archaea**, which scientists believe have unique evolutionary lineages.
 
• **Most prokaryotes **are small,** single-celled organisms** that have a **relatively simple structure**.
 
• **Mesosome **is an **organelle **of **bacteria **that appears as an invagination of the **plasma membrane **and **functions either in DNA replication **and **cell division **or **excretion of exoenzymes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A nucleus**, as related to **genomics**, is the **membrane-enclosed organelle **within **a cell **that **contains the chromosomes**. 
 
• In the **nucleus **of **each cell**, the **DNA molecule **is **packaged **into **thread-like structures **called **chromosomes**.
 
• The **nuclear membrane **is a **double layer **that **encloses **the **cell's nucleus**, where the **chromosomes reside**. The nuclear membrane serves to **separate the chromosomes **from the **cell's cytoplasm **and **other contents**.

questions.question: Which of the following causes enlargement and extension growth of cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turgor pressure.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Enlargement and extension growth of cells is primarily caused by **cell turgor pressure** and **cell wall expansion**.
 
• In plants, this growth is **driven by water uptake**, which increases turgor pressure within the cells, leading to expansion.
 
• Additionally, the synthesis of new cell wall materials allows for **cell elongation.**
 
• Other factors, such as **hormonal regulation** (e.g., auxins), also play a role in promoting cell growth and elongation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Imbibition**

 
 
• It is the process by which a substance (usually a solid, like seeds or plant tissues) **absorbs water and swells.**
 
• This occurs due to the affinity of water molecules for the polar surfaces of the solid. In seeds, imbibition triggers metabolic activities, leading to germination.
 
• **Example**: When dry seeds are placed in water, they absorb water, swell, and become turgid, preparing for germination.
 
 
 
• **Pressure Potential**
 
 
• Pressure potential is the physical pressure exerted by the fluid (usually water) within the cell** against the cell wall.**
 
• In plant cells, when water enters the cell through osmosis, it creates turgor pressure that pushes the plasma membrane against the cell wall, contributing to the overall water potential.
 
• Pressure potential is essential for maintaining cell structure and rigidity, **allowing plants to stand upright and grow.**
 
 
 
• **Osmotic Pressure**
 
 
• It is the pressure required to **prevent the flow of water across a semipermeable membrane **due to osmotic potential (the tendency of water to move into a solution).
 
• It results from differences in solute concentration on either side of a membrane. Water moves from an area of lower solute concentration (higher water potential) to an area of higher solute concentration (lower water potential).
 
• It is crucial for processes like nutrient uptake, cell hydration, and overall water balance in cells and organisms.

questions.question: Which membrane-bound organelles, first discovered in 1857, are often referred to as the 'energy factories' of the cell because they are responsible for making adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the cell's main energy-carrying molecule?
questions.solution:
The corrrect answer is __**Mitochondria.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Mitochondria are frequently called the **“powerhouses” or “energy factories”** of a cell because they are incharge of making **adenosine triphosphate (ATP),** the cell's main energy-carrying molecule.
 
• Mitochondria, frequently referred to as the “powerhouses of the cell”, were first discovered in 1857 by physiologist **Albert von Kolliker**, and later coined** “bioblasts” (life germs) by Richard Altman in 1886.**
 
• **Mitochondria** are **membrane-bound cell organelles** that generate most of the chemical energy needed to power the cell's biochemical reactions.
 
• **Chemical energy produced by the mitochondria** is stored in a small molecule called** adenosine triphosphate (ATP).**

 [IMAGE: https://encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcSNemG45VCVcjwNf41WRaw7-QryDlGReNxX-FPBDk3NRQ&s] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The smooth endoplasmic reticulum functions in many metabolic processes. It **synthesizes lipids, phospholipids as in plasma membranes, and steroids**.
 
• A vacuole is **a membrane-bound cell organelle**. In animal cells, vacuoles are commonly small and help sequester waste products. In plant cells, vacuoles help maintain water balance. Sometimes a single vacuole can take up most of the interior space of the plant cell.
 
• A ribosome is **an intercellular structure made of both RNA and protein, and it is the site of protein synthesis in the cell**.

questions.question: The cell wall of bacteria is made up of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **peptidoglycan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Peptidoglycan is a **polymer that provides structural support** to the bacterial cell wall, helping maintain its shape and integrity.
 
• It is **composed of sugars and amino acids,** forming a mesh-like structure that is unique to bacteria.
 
• The amount and structure of peptidoglycan in the cell wall determine whether bacteria are classified as** Gram-positive or Gram-negative**, affecting their response to antibiotics.
 
• The cell wall protects bacteria from **osmotic pressure and environmental stresses**, making it crucial for their survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glycogen**

 
 
• Glycogen is a storage** form of glucose in animals and fungi,** not found in bacterial cell walls.
 
• It is a polysaccharide composed of glucose units, primarily used for energy storage.
 
 
 
• **Cellulose**
 
 
• Cellulose is a major **component of plant cell walls**, providing structural support.
 
• It is not a structural component of bacterial cell walls.
 
 
 
• **Peptone**
 
 
• Peptone is a **protein digest used in culture media for growing bacteria**, but it is not a component of the bacterial cell wall.
 
• It is made from the digestion of proteins and provides nutrients for bacteria in laboratory settings.

• In insects, **chitin** functions as scaffold material, supporting the cuticles of the epidermis and trachea as well as the peritrophic matrices lining the gut epithelium.
 
• Cellulose is the 30% of a tree that can be made into paper.

• Some MTOCs are:

• Basal body (in cilium)
 
• Spindle pole body (in yeasts)

questions.question: The division of cytoplasm is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cytokinesis**__;

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytokinesis**:-

 
 
• It is a critical step in cell division that follows karyokinesis.
 
• During cytokinesis, the cytoplasm divides into two daughter cells, each with a complete set of chromosomes.
 
• Cytokinesis involves the formation of a contractile ring around the cell, which constricts and separates the cytoplasm into two parts.
 
• The contractile ring is made up of actin and myosin filaments that help in the division of the cytoplasm.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karyokinesis**:-

 
 
• It is the division of the nucleus during cell division.
 
 
 
• **Cytoskeleton**:-
 
 
• It is a network of protein filaments that provide structural support and shape to the cell.
 
 
 
• **Cytosol**:-
 
 
• It is the fluid portion of the cytoplasm that surrounds the organelles.

questions.question: Cytology is related to the study of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytology is the study of individual cells of the body, in contrast to histology which is the study of whole human tissue**__.

 __
 
• The human body is made up of millions of cells and these can be sampled and viewed under a microscope after appropriate preparation to help diagnose medical conditions.
 
• This involves looking at individual cells for abnormal changes in both the nucleus and the cytoplasm (body) of the cell.
 
• The nucleus contains the genetic material that controls the cell and determines what type of cell it will become, but also controls its behavior.
 
• Cytology is widely used in medicine for the prevention and diagnosis of disease.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Robert Hooke was the first scientist to use the word 'cell' in 1665** when he looked at slices of cork through a lit compound microscope and observed very small, irregular boxes that reminded him of tiny rooms, or cells.

 
 
• Hooke wrote about his findings and drew the structures he saw in his book Micrographia, which was published in 1665.
 
 
 
• The earliest cell theory was developed in 1838 by plant scientist Matthias Schleiden and animal scientist **Theodor Schwann.**
 
• They each came to the same conclusion that the living things they studied were composed of cells.

• Primary types of body tissues include epithelial, connective, muscular, and nervous tissues.

questions.question: In animal cells, which membrane-bound cell organelles are generally smaller and help to separate waste products?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vacuoles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A vacuole **is a **membrane-bound cell organelle**.
 
• In **animal cells**, **vacuoles **are generally **small **and **help sequester waste products**.
 
• In **plant cells**, vacuoles **help maintain water balance**.
 
• **Sometimes **a **single vacuole **can take **up most of the interior space **of the **plant cell**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plastids**__

 __
 
• **Plastids **are **double-membrane organelles **that are **found **in the **cells of plants and algae**.
 
• **Plastids **are responsible for manufacturing and **storing food**.
 
 
 
• **Cytosols**__
 __
 
• The **cytosol **is the **liquid medium contained **within a cell.
 
• The **cytosol **is a **component of the cytoplasm**.
 
 
 
• **Golgi apparatus**__
 
 
• The **Golgi apparatus**, also known as the **Golgi complex**, **Golgi body**, or simply the **Golgi**, is an **organelle **found in **most eukaryotic cells**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about mitochondria?

options.text: Mitochondria is present only in bacteria.
Mitochondria is present in all living cells.
Mitochondria is not bound by any membrane.
Mitochondria without outer membrane is called mitoplast.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Mitochondria without outer membrane is called mitoplast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria**__

 __
 
• All **eukaryotic cells have mitochondria**, which are **double membrane-bound organelles** that generate a**denosine triphosphate (ATP), the primary energy source required by the cell**.
 
• It is commonly known as the** "Powerhouse of the cell."**
 
• Both** plant and animal cells contain **the double-membraned, rod-shaped **mitochondria**.
 
• Its diameter varies from **0.5 to 1.0 micrometres**.
 
• The structure is made up of an **inner membrane, an outer membrane, cisternae, the intermembrane space and matrix**.
 
• The quantity of mitochondria **differs from cell to cell**.
 
• **RBC which is a type of living cell lacks mitochondria**, whereas liver cells have about 2000 per cell.
 
• In contrast to eukaryotes, **bacteria do not have membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria** or chloroplasts.
 
• Mitochondria without an **outer membrane are called mitoplast**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The mitochondria also perform **signaling, cellular differentiation, cell death, and maintenance of cell cycle growth**.
 
• Mitochondria have their **own genetic material**.
 
• The i**ntermembrane space serves as a barrier between the layers of proteins and phospholipids that make up the outer membrane and the inner membrane**.
 
• The mitochondrion's **outer membrane** is made up of** numerous unique proteins called porins and covers its surface**. 
 
• The** genome of human mitochondria** is **circular DNA**.

questions.question: Plant cells differ from animal cells in having an additional layer around the cell membrane termed as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Cell wall.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The cell wall is present in plant cells but not in animal cells and it is made up of **cellulose and chitin.**
 
• The plant is covered by an outer cell wall.
 
• **Cellulose is one of the major components of the cell wall.**
 
• It is a polymer of glucose joined by glycosidic linkage.
 
• **It helps in maintaining its shape and provides rigidity to the plant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

**Mitochondria:**

 
• **Mitochondria is a double-layered cell organelle, **in which the outer layer is porous and the inner layer is folded upon itself is known to be **cristae.**
 
• The number of mitochondria in a single cell may be up to 50 to 5000.
 
• The inner lumen of mitochondria contains ribosome phosphate particles and** DNA **molecules.
 
• It has the potential to synthesize its own protein and the oxidation of carbohydrates and fats are taken place with the help of enzymes in mitochondria.
 
• This energy is stored in the form of **ATP **( Adenosine Triphosphate ) so, these are known as the "Powerhouse of the cell".

**Golgi apparatus:**

 
• **This cell organelle is primarily responsible for the storage, processing, and packaging of proteins.**
 
• Golgi Apparatus is found within the cytoplasm of a cell and are present in both plant and animal cells.

**Ribosomes:**

 
• The eukaryotic cell comprises of true nucleus and organelles in its cytoplasm.
 
• Mitochondria, ribosomes, Endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi complex are organelles present in the cytoplasm.
 
• **The sites for protein synthesis in the cells are ribosomes.**
 
• **Ribosomes are present as free ribosomes in the cytoplasm or, as membrane-bound on the rough endoplasmic reticulum.**
 
• Ribosomes consist of small and large subunits and are 80s-type.
 
• It is the site where **mRNA translation **occurs, and protein formation takes place.

questions.question: A part of the cell other than the nucleus which has DNA and ribosomes and can thus make its own proteins is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mitochondria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they produce energy in the form of ATP through the process of oxidative phosphorylation.
 
• They contain their own DNA, which is separate from the nuclear DNA, and ribosomes, which allows them to synthesize some of their own proteins.
 
• Mitochondria are involved in various cellular processes, including the regulation of the cell cycle and cell growth.
 
• They are found in almost all eukaryotic cells, and their number can vary depending on the energy requirements of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**

 
 
• ER is a network of membranes found throughout the cell and connected to the nucleus.
 
• There are two types of ER: Rough ER (with ribosomes attached) and Smooth ER (without ribosomes).
 
• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and quality control, while Smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes**
 
 
• Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.
 
• They can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the Rough ER.
 
• Ribosomes are composed of RNA and proteins and are critical for translating mRNA into functional proteins.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus**
 
 
• The Golgi apparatus is a series of stacked membranes involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• It is often considered the cell's "post office" due to its role in trafficking molecules to their appropriate destinations.

questions.question: Choose the correct sequence for central dogma.

options.text: Protein translation, DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription
DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription, Protein translation
m-RNA transcription, Protein translation, DNA Replication
m-RNA transcription, DNA Replication, Protein translation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA Replication, mRNA transcription, Protein translation .**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **process by which DNA is copied to RNA** is called **transcription**, and that by which **RNA is used to produce proteins** is called **translation**.
 
• The major steps of transcription are **initiation, promoter clearance, elongation, and termination**.
 
• Essentially, what happens during transcription is that **an mRNA “copies down” the instructions for making a protein** from DNA.
 
• DNA replication is the **process by which the genome's DNA is copied** in cells.
 
• The process of translation can be seen as the **decoding of instructions for making proteins**, involving mRNA in transcription as well as tRNA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d885884d008aeffbc804c583f27ef2d3ddc6211d497e2cec58bbdc89d987e9ed.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Deoxyribonucleic acid (abbreviated DNA) is the **molecule that carries genetic information** for the development and functioning of an organism.
 
• Ribonucleic acid (abbreviated RNA) is a **nucleic acid present in all living cells** that has structural similarities to DNA.
 
• **Proteins** are made up of hundreds or thousands of **smaller units called amino acids**, which are **attached to one another in long chains**.
 
• Proteins are **20 different types of amino acids** that can be combined to make a protein.
